contents.text:
I'm keeping the answer brief and leading with it, pointing to the ADR at src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md. I'll offer a few follow-up choices instead of showing a page, since I don't know the exact address of the packs section on /how-it-works and would need to look it up first.

Next I'm settling on the writing style for the reply: short sentences, prose for any explanation, with lists kept only for steps or choices.

ADR 0027 decides that the engine names no product. Core holds the loop, sessions, usage, guards and the tools every agent needs. Products are configured as identities and packs instead of being built into core.

An identity (`IAgentIdentity`) says who an agent is: its voice, modes, roles, and which packs it uses. Puls, the demo, the coding agent and voorman are all identities.

A pack (`IAgentPack`) says what an agent can do: toolsets, providers, guides, settings, and the packs it requires. A pack never references another pack or an identity. An identity may contain workflow code that uses its own packs' public types.

A single composition project, `src/hosts/LouisAgent.Composition`, knows every identity and pack. A host picks them at start-up with `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS`, and the catalog is passed down as an object, not a static.

The reason is that Puls had grown into core. Its prompts, shop tools and South African time zone default lived there, so every product carried Puls. The ADR also rejected loading packs as DLLs from a folder, because that would put someone else's code inside the process.

Consequences: a new identity or pack adds no branch to core. Core's time zone now comes from `HOST_TIME_ZONE`. Identities and packs load only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change mid-session.
